title: The idea of a jazz repertory
summary: Problems of recreating old Ellington and other music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: If you don't mind, I'd like to talk a little bit about what we were discussing earlier, about the whole idea of a jazz repertory. Would you be interested in talking about that?
Sure, if what I say has any value.

I think so. We were discussing earlier something about the current trend in going back and playing works that were done maybe thirty or forty years ago, and we were talking, for example, about playing the Sauter-Finegan music or playing Ellington works from the early forties of playing King Oliver's things, or whomever. In other words, trying to go back and recreate
styles from the past and the problems that are associated with that kind of approach.

We discussed a little bit about the problems, for example, of whether or not you should go back and try to play old Ellington music that was written for specific people like a Hodges, and you had mixed feelings about that.

One thing was because of the people you named, the Hodges and Carney, who they were written for, it was what those people were at the time it was done. Their whole lifestyle, everything around them, the way they dressed, the food they ate, how they procured that food, what it really felt like to be a part of the society of say, 1936. It was another world and we can't possibly know that.
All we can know is certain technical attitudes and what we've been told about that period, but one has to
really consider who has been doing the telling. Too often it's critics and my observation of critics is not that perceptive. They usually set up a point that is easily proved and let it go at that.

If you take that as our point of departure, we are likely to get in trouble. Maybe I'm being a little hard on critics but I don't always mean the critics who write reviews. It could be anyone who is discussing the period, including me.
